title: A tensor power of a section lifts across a square-zero immersion
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of locally Noetherian, quasi-compact schemes [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on $X$ and let $I=j.\ker$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] have $I^2=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Write $P=j^*$ for tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], with the canonical adjunction unit $\eta$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For any $n\ge0$, global section $s$ of $N=(P L)^{\otimes n}$ and affine open $U\subset Z$ equal as a set to the nonvanishing locus of $s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], there are $k>0$, a global section $t$ of $L^{\otimes nk}$, and a module isomorphism $e:P(L^{\otimes nk})\simeq N^{\otimes k}$ such that the section morphism associated to $\eta_{L^{\otimes nk}}(t)$, followed by $e$, equals the $k$th tensor power of the section morphism associated to $s$. The section morphism sends $1$ to its given global section. No nonvanishing-locus comparison is part of the conclusion.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Put N=j^*L. The closed-immersion ideal sequence tensored by the invertible L^d is exact, with kernel M_d=I tensor L^d and quotient j_*j^*(L^d), by the unit-quotient theorem. Pullback commutes with tensors, so identify the quotient with j_*(N^d). The ideal I and M_d are quasi-coherent, and I M_d=0 because I^2=0. The annihilated-module theorem identifies M_d with j_*G_d, where G_d=j^*M_d is quasi-coherent. The affine-morphism cohomology edge identifies H^1(X,M_d) with H^1(Z,G_d). The given section s of N^n has a connecting class xi in degree n.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Set O'=direct sum over m>=0 of L^{tensor m} and O=direct sum over m>=0 of j_*j^*L^{tensor m}, with multiplication by tensor product. These are sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras: locally a frame for the invertible L identifies O' with a polynomial algebra in one generator, so its multiplication is commutative; the quotient O is commutative too. The degreewise surjection from step 1 gives O' \to O with kernel K=direct sum over m>=0 of I tensor L^{tensor m}; products of two kernel terms land in I^2 tensor L^{tensor (a+b)}=0. Apply [lem-sc-boundary-derivation-square-zero] to O' \to O. By naturality of the long exact sequence for inclusion of a degree-m summand and projection onto it, projecting the boundary of the summed sequence to degree m is the boundary of the degree-m exact sequence. Thus the image of s in the degree-n summand has boundary xi. Induct on k>=1: for k=1 this is xi; if partial(s^k)=k s^{k-1}xi, the Leibniz rule gives partial(s^{k+1})=s partial(s^k)+s^k partial(s)=(k+1)s^k xi. Taking k=e+1 gives partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi, where s^e acts through O on K.

Use the given affine open U=Z_s. Apply the affine-open killing theorem on Z to N^n, s, G_n, p=1, and xi under the edge comparison. Z is quasi-compact and is quasi-separated by local Noetherianity. It gives e with s^e xi=0. Naturality of the edge comparison for the map G_n -> G_n tensor (N^n)^e, v -> v tensor s^e, identifies this with the degree-ne action on H^1(X,M_n). Therefore the preceding derivation formula gives partial(s^(e+1))=0. Exactness lifts s^(e+1) to t in Gamma(X,L^(n*(e+1))); use the tensor-power multiplication isomorphism to put its degree in that order. Set k=e+1, so k>0.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Iterate the tensor-pullback comparisons, using the monoidal unit comparison in degree zero and associators for tensor powers, to obtain e: j^*(L^(n*k)) isomorphic to ((j^*L)^n)^k. Their section formulas identify the restricted lift with the pure tensor power of s. The equivalence of structure-module morphisms and global sections turns this equality into the stated equality of morphisms.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 09MS, tensor exact sequence and boundary calculation; ends with the lift, before the comparison of nonvanishing opens

theorem exists_section_power_lift_of_square_zero
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Z] [CompactSpace Z]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ) (s : (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj
      (Opposite.op ⊤)) (U : Z.Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set Z) = nonvanishingLocus (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n) s)
    (hAffine : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧
      ∃ t : (L.tensorPow (n * k)).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤),
        ∃ e : (tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * k)) ≅
            (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).tensorPow k,
          homOfGlobalSection ((tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * k)))
              (((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j)).unit.app
                (L.tensorPow (n * k))).val.app (Opposite.op ⊤) t) ≫ e.hom =
            tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection
              (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n) s) k
